start.text: Porchlight wants to welcome her back. Before we do, can you tell me what this account actually proves?

choices.label: What do you miss about her? [Interviewing 2]

sources.text: Start with the summary and the badge’s scope. Everyone keeps showing me one as if it were the other. I’ve left both at Porchlight.

why.text: Because everyone else has already chosen which answer they need. I want the deception challenged. I also miss the place we were before it needed a moderator every six minutes.

choices.label: I can investigate. I can’t promise comfort.

miss.text: She noticed when somebody went quiet. Not their engagement rate. Them. A community can give real care and still tell itself a convenient lie.

start.text: Use the public records. Leave my message and the private trace out of the packet. Can you promise that?

choices.label: I will keep that private context out of the packet.
I can’t promise what the packet will contain yet.
What would an honest boundary sound like? [Interviewing 3]

promise.text: Then make that boundary mean something when the packet is in front of you. Reading a message is not permission to circulate it.

decline.text: Then say so when you decide. Don’t let a label make the choice for you. You may read my consented message to Rafi; that is not permission to send people looking.

boundary.text: Say who receives it. Say what they can keep. “Safe” is not a destination. “Private” is not the same as leaving it out.

start.text: A coherent account is useful. Its omissions are less visible. Bring me two passages and tell me exactly what does not follow.

scope.text: A credential chain belongs to an account. A claim about its operator needs other evidence. Similarity does not change the question a test can answer.

start.text: The Warden enforces the mandate in front of them. An account badge is not a mandate to inspect the service behind it.

scope.text: The Oracle identifies a provenance question. This office authorises a scoped review. The Warden applies that scope. None of these roles certifies a life.
